options.text: Any substance that can be dissolved in water
A substance that releases energy (usually by combustion) when it reacts with oxygen
A substance that absorbs energy from the environment
A substance that does not react with anything

questions.explanation: A fuel is a substance that reacts with oxygen to release useful energy, usually as heat and light. Most fuels release energy through combustion (burning). Common fuels include methane, petrol, coal, and hydrogen.

questions.stem: What are the products of the complete combustion of a hydrocarbon fuel?

options.text: Carbon monoxide and water
Carbon dioxide and water
Carbon and hydrogen
Carbon dioxide and hydrogen

questions.explanation: Complete combustion of a hydrocarbon (containing carbon and hydrogen only) in excess oxygen produces carbon dioxide and water. For example: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O.

questions.stem: Why is the combustion of fuels described as exothermic?

options.text: Because it requires a continuous supply of heat
Because it releases more energy when making bonds in the products than is needed to break bonds in the reactants
Because it always produces a gas
Because it involves oxygen

questions.explanation: Combustion is exothermic because the energy released when forming the new bonds in CO₂ and H₂O is greater than the energy required to break the bonds in the fuel and oxygen molecules. The overall result is a net release of energy.

questions.stem: Which environmental problem is caused by the carbon dioxide released from burning fossil fuels?

options.text: Acid rain
Ozone layer depletion
Climate change (global warming) due to the enhanced greenhouse effect
Water pollution

questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide is a greenhouse gas. Increased levels of CO₂ from burning fossil fuels enhance the greenhouse effect, trapping more heat in the atmosphere and contributing to climate change and global warming.

questions.stem: What is produced during incomplete combustion of a hydrocarbon fuel?

options.text: Only carbon dioxide and water
Carbon monoxide and/or carbon (soot), along with water
Hydrogen and oxygen
Only water

questions.explanation: When there is insufficient oxygen for complete combustion, incomplete combustion occurs. This produces carbon monoxide (a toxic gas) and/or carbon particulates (soot), along with water. Less energy is released than in complete combustion.

questions.stem: Why is hydrogen considered a clean fuel?

options.text: Because it is cheap to produce
Because the only product of its combustion is water, with no carbon dioxide produced
Because it is found naturally in large quantities
Because it burns at a low temperature

questions.explanation: Hydrogen is considered a clean fuel because when it burns, the only product is water: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O. No carbon dioxide or other pollutants are produced at the point of use, making it environmentally friendly.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a disadvantage of using fossil fuels?

options.text: They release no energy when burned
They are renewable and will never run out
They are non-renewable, produce greenhouse gases, and can cause air pollution
They are too expensive to extract from the ground

questions.explanation: Fossil fuels (coal, oil, natural gas) are non-renewable, meaning they will eventually run out. Burning them produces carbon dioxide (contributing to climate change), and can also produce sulfur dioxide (acid rain), nitrogen oxides, and particulates (air pollution).
